{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "Sjors",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK with caveats; objects to stopping on mismatch as an effective checkpoint, suggests keeping older commitments, and asks about flushing"
    },
    {
      "login": "optout21",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; suggests an option to skip the check and keeping older commitments for visibility"
    },
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objects that crashing IBD on mismatch makes bad snapshot releases worse for everyone, asks about performance impact, and suggests alternative approaches"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:6229005853",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Stopping the node on a mismatch risks introducing an effective checkpoint that prevents normal sync if the snapshot commitment is malicious",
      "quote": "I think this risks introducing a new effective checkpoint. If the snapshot were malicious, normal users couldn't sync",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6229005853",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Limit the scope of the PR by checking the latest hash without deleting the older commitments yet",
      "quote": "Maybe limit the scope of this PR by only _checking_ the latest hash, but not (yet) deleting the other hashes.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6229005853",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Provide benchmark numbers in the PR description showing minimal performance impact",
      "quote": "It would be good to provide some numbers in the PR description.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6229005853",
      "part": 4,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "How does flushing chainstate to disk before hashing interact with current IBD flush frequency?",
      "quote": "I'm not up to speed on how often and when we flush the chainstate to disk during IBD nowadays. How does this interact with that?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6230060049",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Add a configuration option to bypass or ignore the AssumeUTXO hash check",
      "quote": "Introduce an option to skip the new AssumeUTXO hash check (may be a hidden option)",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6230060049",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Keep non-latest AssumeUTXO commitments in source for visibility instead of dropping them",
      "quote": "So not checking the non-latest hashes is fine, but it's useful to keep them for visibility.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6379792380",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "What is the performance impact when hitting an AssumeUTXO commitment block during validation?",
      "quote": "What's the performance impact when hitting such a block?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6379792380",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Crashing an IBD node on snapshot mismatch penalizes nodes with fully verified valid data while failing to protect snapshot users from following an incorrect chain",
      "quote": "Doesn't this make the result of a release including bad snaphot data worse for everyone -- Alice who does IBD has her node crash despite having good data that she fully verified, and Bob who uses the bad snapshot still potentially fails to an incorrect chain",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6379792380",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Consider predictable snapshot points (e.g. BIP 452) or including the block's muhash in the AssumeUTXO commitment to make verification easier and less disruptive",
      "quote": "Having predictable snapshot points (every 14112 blocks [per bip452]) would allow every node to calculate the appropriate hash... Including the block's muhash in the assumeutxo set would also probably work here",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",

      "author_replies": [],

      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],

}

participants.note: Concept ACK with caveats; objects to stopping on mismatch as an effective checkpoint, suggests keeping older commitments, and asks about flushing
Concept ACK; suggests an option to skip the check and keeping older commitments for visibility
objects that crashing IBD on mismatch makes bad snapshot releases worse for everyone, asks about performance impact, and suggests alternative approaches

claims.text: Stopping the node on a mismatch risks introducing an effective checkpoint that prevents normal sync if the snapshot commitment is malicious
claims.quote: I think this risks introducing a new effective checkpoint. If the snapshot were malicious, normal users couldn't sync

claims.text: Limit the scope of the PR by checking the latest hash without deleting the older commitments yet
claims.quote: Maybe limit the scope of this PR by only _checking_ the latest hash, but not (yet) deleting the other hashes.

claims.text: Provide benchmark numbers in the PR description showing minimal performance impact
claims.quote: It would be good to provide some numbers in the PR description.

claims.text: How does flushing chainstate to disk before hashing interact with current IBD flush frequency?
claims.quote: I'm not up to speed on how often and when we flush the chainstate to disk during IBD nowadays. How does this interact with that?

claims.text: Add a configuration option to bypass or ignore the AssumeUTXO hash check
claims.quote: Introduce an option to skip the new AssumeUTXO hash check (may be a hidden option)

claims.text: Keep non-latest AssumeUTXO commitments in source for visibility instead of dropping them
claims.quote: So not checking the non-latest hashes is fine, but it's useful to keep them for visibility.

claims.text: What is the performance impact when hitting an AssumeUTXO commitment block during validation?
claims.quote: What's the performance impact when hitting such a block?

claims.text: Crashing an IBD node on snapshot mismatch penalizes nodes with fully verified valid data while failing to protect snapshot users from following an incorrect chain
claims.quote: Doesn't this make the result of a release including bad snaphot data worse for everyone -- Alice who does IBD has her node crash despite having good data that she fully verified, and Bob who uses the bad snapshot still potentially fails to an incorrect chain

claims.text: Consider predictable snapshot points (e.g. BIP 452) or including the block's muhash in the AssumeUTXO commitment to make verification easier and less disruptive
claims.quote: Having predictable snapshot points (every 14112 blocks [per bip452]) would allow every node to calculate the appropriate hash... Including the block's muhash in the assumeutxo set would also probably work here

support.reason: As there is a hash provided that requires trust, the more checks the better. It makes sense to use all nodes performing IBD to also perform this check, as it's relatively cheap to do.

result.notes: Added ajtowns with three items (a question on performance impact, an objection regarding crashing nodes during IBD when snapshot data is bad, and a suggestion for alternative snapshot designs such as predictable points or muhash).
